scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance originated from the Lindy Hop, which appeared around 1920, and evolved through the Boogie Woogie of the 1940s.
By 1955, as rock music gained popularity, the dance form began to shift toward a more competitive, acrobatic style.
In the 1970s, French dance schools in Lyon helped formalize the discipline, leading to the creation of the World Rock'N'Roll Confederation (WRRC).
on_screen: Map: United States (origin), France (modern sport development) · Europe
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Acrobatic Rock'n'Roll is primarily a competitive sport.
It is performed at local, national, and international championships organized by the WRRC.
The focus is on precision, athleticism, and the successful execution of high-difficulty acrobatic elements.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance relies on a 6-basic or 9-basic step structure.
The 9-basic step is the modern tournament standard, characterized by a 'kick-ball-change' maneuver.
Dancers move in a linear fashion, maintaining a precise, upright posture while executing kicks into the air.
Watch for Einsteiger, Körperwelle.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (uvbLjBYyQ3c)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Linear movement, pairs or formation groups.
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance is performed to 4/4 time music, typically modern disco or pop tracks played at high speeds between 176 and 208 bpm.
The rhythm emphasizes the first and third beats of each measure, differing from the off-beat stress found in traditional rock music.
Listen for the Modern pop/disco instrumentation.
The pulse is 4/4 at about 192 beats a minute.
High-tempo, driving beat with a clear, consistent pulse designed to support rapid footwork and athletic movement.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Dancers wear custom-made, multicoloured costumes crafted from elastic, durable artificial fibers.
These are designed to be tight-fitting to prevent snagging during acrobatics.
Footwear consists of light jazz shoes for dance programs or aerobics sneakers for acrobatic programs to provide grip and shock absorption.
